text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The Oslo Bourse hit a record high twelve times in November. The Total share index rose 7.1 percent in the month.

- Eleven hospitals in northern Norway are cooperating together to try and recruit 120 doctors. Last weekend they held a doctor's fair in Stockholm, Sweden. Tor Oeyvind, head of information at Regionssykehuset in Tromsoe, says the first Swedish doctor may arrive in Tromsoe in just a few days.

- Oil company Saga Petroleum ASA has won the takeover battle for British-based Santa Fe Exploration. Saga will pay $1.2 billion for the North Sea explorer. Norwegian analysts wonder if the price is too high.

- Brokerhouse Fondsfinans recommends buying shares in tanker shipping company Nordic American Shipping ASA (NAS). Fondsfinans says increased oil production and start up of several small oil fields has led to good business opportunities for NAS.

- Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo wants to merge Norwegian defence companies Kongsberg Gruppen ASA og Raufoss AS. In addition, Kosmo and the Swedish Defence Minister Thage Peterson want the Norwegian companies to work closer with Swedish industry.
